previous_statement: Affine pairing: if h is affine and sum_j P_vj=1, then h(sum_j P_vj p_j)=sum_j P_vj h(p_j). Combining this with p_v=sum_j P_vj p_j and admissibility h(p_v)=0 from def-exposed gives 0=sum_j P_vj h(p_j).
new_statement: Affine pairing fact: if h is affine, a_j are real coefficients with finite support, and sum_j a_j=1, then h(sum_j a_j p_j)=sum_j a_j h(p_j). In particular this applies to a_j=P_vj once sum_j P_vj=1 is known.
